title: Per-route telemetry and cost tracing for semantic-search pipeline
creator: Katherine Li
description: Add per-route telemetry, distributed tracing, and cost-attribution for the full semantic-search pipeline (embed -> ANN search -> rerank scoring) so product owners can answer: why is latency/cost/spike happening for a specific customer route? This work creates fine-grained spans, route tagging, and a dashboard set + alerting that attributes token and compute cost to routes and model variants.
background: Current dashboards show node-level and model-wide metrics. We lack per-route breakdowns and traces that connect embedding latency, nearest-neighbor search time, and reranker scoring. On a recent incident a single high-cardinality route caused tail-latency regressions and cost overruns but was hard to isolate. Engineering and PM asked for route-level visibility and automated alerts tied to cost thresholds.
goals: Emit route_id and model_variant as stable attributes on all spans and metrics
Instrument three pipeline segments with spans: embedding generation, ANN search, rerank scoring
Create Grafana dashboards with panels for per-route P50/P95/P99 latency, per-route cost per 1000 requests, and token-unit breakdown
Add alerting rules for route-level latency SLO violations and cost anomalies
Ensure traces avoid logging or exporting user PII/text (sampling + redaction)
non_goals: Re-architect ANN service or change underlying reranker model quality
Full retroactive cost attribution for historical data beyond 30 days
Capture full request payloads in traces (we will only store metadata and token counts)
success_metrics: Mean time to identify root cause for route-level incidents reduced from 3 hours to <30 minutes
Per-route cost attribution coverage >= 95% for requests routed through hosted inference
Dashboards and alerts adopted by 3 customer-facing PMs within first 2 weeks
No increase in PII exposure incidents after rollout
design_decisions: Use OpenTelemetry for distributed tracing and propagate a stable trace.route_id tag across services
Add three canonical span names: emb.generate, ann.search, rerank.score
Record numeric metrics: token_count, input_seq_len, kv_cache_hit, model_flops_estimate for cost estimation
Sampling strategy: 1% default sample, 10% for routes with >10k qps, and forced sample on alerts
Avoid exporting raw request text. Only send hashed request_id and token counts to observability backends
implementation_tasks: Runtime: add span start/end hooks around embedding generation with route_id and model_variant tags
ANN service: add timing spans and expose per-search candidate counts; tag with shard_id and route_id
Reranker: instrument tokenized scoring, record rerank_time and rerank_model_variant
Telemetry: map token_count -> billing units using current pricing table and emit cost_estimate metric
Tracing infra: update OTLP exporter config and add sampling rules; ensure trace IDs are consistent across services
Dashboards: create per-route dashboard template panels (latency, error rate, cost per 1k requests, tokens per request)
Alerting: add prom-alert rules for route-level P99 > 500ms for >5m and cost spike > 3x baseline in 15m
Privacy: implement redaction hooks to strip text fields before sending traces/metrics
Backfill: run daily batch to join traces and billing rows for initial 30-day attribution window
QA: integration tests for span propagation, end-to-end synthetic traffic across 3 representative routes
acceptance_criteria: Spans with names emb.generate, ann.search, rerank.score appear in traces for sampled requests
Every emitted span includes route_id, model_variant, and request_token_count tags
Grafana dashboard shows per-route P95/P99 latency and cost panels; dashboards accept route_id as template variable
Alerts trigger in staging when synthetic route latency/cost thresholds are crossed and create tickets automatically
No trace or metric contains actual user text payloads (verified by logging audit)
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary): roll instrumentation to 10% of traffic for low-risk routes for 48 hours
Stage 2 (expanded): enable per-route sampling and dashboards for all hosted routes; monitor storage impact for 7 days
Stage 3 (GA): flip default sampling to 0.5% and enable alerting rules for all routes; ship dashboard templates to Console
Rollback: disable exporter + sampling rules if observability storage exceeds budget or privacy concerns are detected
risks_and_mitigations: Increased observability storage costs: mitigate with lower default sampling and host-side aggregation of cost_estimate metrics
PII leakage risk: enforce redaction hooks and automated scanning of traces before export
Metric cardinality explosion (route_id high-cardinality): add route_id cardinality bucketing and use rate-limited label cardinality in Prometheus
Query perf regressions in Grafana: use pre-aggregated rollup tables for 1h/6h/24h windows
notes: This ticket focuses on visibility and attribution rather than optimization. After this ships we'll evaluate targeted batching or routing changes based on observed hotspots.
